crime_highlights: Mr. McCook unlawfully discharged a loaded firearm from inside his and Ms. Poole's residence toward a parked vehicle
One of the bullets struck Ms. Poole, who was seated in the passenger seat of the vehicle, in the head, causing her death.
Mr. McCook consumed very large quantities of alcohol and became profoundly intoxicated
rationale_highlights: the Indigenous Sentencing Report similarly demonstrates that Mr. McCook's early removal from family, intergenerational trauma, and normalization of alcohol misuse formed part of the broader context in which his substance dependency developed
they inform the assessment of moral blameworthiness
a modest downward adjustment to the lower end of the applicable range is justified

crime_highlights: Moments later, the vehicle suddenly burst into flames.
The man (who was later identified as Mr. Craig) immediately fled the area on foot.
the pursuing officer was certain that Mr. Craig was the same individual he observed setting the Ford F350 on fire
The arson occurred in a public place, during daylight hours, in a residential area, near a school. The potential for harm to persons or nearby property was substantial.
rationale_highlights: I have also considered Mr. Craig's circumstances as an Indigenous offender.
These factors provide important context in assessing his moral blameworthiness
These background factors inform Mr. Craig's moral blameworthiness and the appropriate balance among sentencing objectives
these factors support a sentence that leaves appropriate room for rehabilitation
